subject: English
passage: Neuromorphic chips process sensor data on-device by mimicking neural circuitry, eliminating the need to transmit inputs to distant servers. The onboard computing of an autonomous drone, for example, can classify obstacles using such chips. A newly designed neuromorphic chip incorporating a dense memristor array has been shown to deliver ultra-low inference latency under real-time workloads, an absolute prerequisite for autonomous drones to navigate unfamiliar environments using on-device computation.
prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the text's claim about autonomous drones?

choices.A: Delayed or unpredictable inference responses prevent autonomous drones from reliably avoiding obstacles during flight.
choices.B: The continuous sensor streams generated by autonomous drones make it possible to guide their navigation using only non-memristor neuromorphic chips.
choices.C: The memristor array is incompatible with most autonomous drone platforms.
choices.D: The density of the memristor array is what allows a neuromorphic chip to classify a sufficient variety of obstacles for autonomous drones.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it presents a finding that, if true, would most directly support the text's claim about autonomous drones. The text states that the newly designed neuromorphic chip delivers 'ultra-low inference latency under real-time workloads, an absolute prerequisite for autonomous drones to navigate unfamiliar environments.' This claim emphasizes that ultra-low latency is necessary for drone navigation. If it is true that delayed or unpredictable inference responses prevent drones from reliably avoiding obstacles, that finding would directly support the claim by explaining why ultra-low latency is an absolute prerequisite: without rapid, reliable inference, drones cannot navigate safely.
